newsitem.title: UK: UK pharmacists may get wider dispensing powers.
newsitem.headline: UK pharmacists may get wider dispensing powers.

text.p: British Health Secretary Frank Dobson is considering giving pharmacists wider powers to dispense drugs without a doctor's prescription, the Financial Times said on Monday.
Health officials believed Dobson was keen to consider proposals from major pharmacy chains, including providing an alternative service for minor health ailments.

The chains want a set of limited medical conditions that could be diagnosed in a pharmacy and treated using a finite number of medicines. These could include asthma and eye or skin conditions, but not anti-depressants or narcotics.
Such a policy move could cut as much as four billion pounds from the National Health Service drugs bill, said the report.
